_comment: Zenodo metadata. Connect the repository under Settings > Repositories on zenodo.org,
then pushing a GitHub release mints a versioned DOI with no further work here.
Publishing this file directly instead gives a snapshot DOI.
This is deliberately visible JSON with no comments stripped, so a human can
audit exactly what a crawler will be handed.
Cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321578, not a version DOI. The concept
DOI always resolves to the newest version, so it stays correct as new versions
are published; a version DOI pins a reader to one immutable snapshot.
The licence is split on purpose. The paper is CC-BY-4.0, which is what the
first published version carries. The code and documentation in LICENSE stay
MIT. tools/check_metadata.py fails if the two are collapsed into one.
Zenodo reads this file against the legacy deposit schema, which is what its
GitHub integration is documented for. Three consequences worth keeping:
- The resource type is the legacy pair upload_type + publication_type.
Publishing this file directly does not read the InvenioRDM spelling
resource_type.id, and a record that falls back to the default lands as a
Report rather than an Article.
- A creator is written 'Family, Given'. A bare 'Huan Li' is parsed with the
whole string as the family name, and that family name then propagates
into DataCite, Crossref and every authority file built from this record.
- version overrides the tag. If it disagrees with the GitHub tag, Zenodo
records the version from this file rather than the release, and the two
then disagree silently. Check them by hand before publishing; the gate
script has no access to the remote tag list.
title: Two saturating operators: non-substitutability of human and machine contribution in AI-assisted discovery
description:
How much did AI contribute is normally answered with a percentage, and the percentage quietly presupposes that human and machine work can be measured in one currency. We formalize the alternative. The two parties act on different variables, and each saturates on a different axis. Holding the hypothesis space fixed, a machine reduces a residual toward a floor Φ that it cannot pass, so its total gain is bounded by log(e₀/Φ) and does not improve with additional inference steps; a human moves the floor itself, and that gain is unbounded. Two further saturations fall out of the same currency. Headcount saturates immediately, because under a max-type coalition the marginal member earns exactly zero while costing strictly more. Corpus size saturates too, because only the single item certifying the lowest floor determines the bound that is attainable at all. A tagged corpus adds a third: the floor function provably never reads the source label, so a provenance tag cannot certify a bound, and one machine item below the human floor takes the bound over however much human material surrounds it.

All of it is proved in Lean 4 (v4.15.0) against Mathlib: 164 theorems and 20 worked examples across thirteen modules, zero sorry, and no axioms beyond Classical.choice, Quot.sound and propext. The sources are in this record and build with lake build, and tools/audit_axioms.py prints the axiom dependencies of every declaration. Machine checking was not a formality. It falsified a confusion-matrix inequality from an earlier draft, forced a total-variation floor into the residual term, reversed two monotonicity directions we had asserted, and refuted one of our own claims on first attempt. Those reversals are reported in the paper, not patched out quietly.

The limits are stated rather than left implicit. The theorems concern a model, not a measurement of the world. The model commits to a max-type coalition, to a corpus read as a set rather than a stream with recency and re-weighting, and to a positive floor Φ that no theorem here establishes. Articulability, meaning whether a tacit piece of knowledge can be written down at all, has no representation at this level, so the tacit-knowledge filter cannot be stated as a theorem. The detection theory and the calibration non-identifiability result sit underneath the main claim, and are what make the machine-side ceiling checkable instead of rhetorical.
